problem: Urban navigation VLA models are trained on limited teleoperated data or sim data with a sim-to-real gap, built around predefined tasks and scenarios, so they cannot reveal which rare or hard situations bottleneck performance. Prior in-the-wild video work gives only high-level decisions or limited-scale (CityWalker ~200h, single city) trajectories, and long-tail studies rely on predefined corner-case taxonomies.
motivation: Progress in urban navigation depends on whether training data cover the situations that limit model performance, not just on more samples. Web-scale egocentric walking videos capture naturally occurring situations, so they can serve both as scalable supervision and as an empirical distribution for jointly analysing rarity and model-dependent difficulty.
key_idea: Automatically convert ~500h of worldwide street-walking videos into metric trajectories plus perception-analysis-planning CoT annotations to train a reasoning-aware VLA (WILD-Nav), then expose the long tail via rarity (IDF over perception-motion features) crossed with model error (ADE/FDE) and privileged teacher reflection for failure attribution.
insight: Rarity and difficulty overlap only partially (24.18% of hard episodes are rare; 14.48% of rare episodes are hard), so they are complementary axes, and failures cluster by scene type (e.g. dense pedestrians -> planning errors, traffic signs -> rule violations). Fine-tuning ablation shows hard examples give targeted tail gains but hurt overall performance (Test-all ADE 0.094 -> 0.121), and mixing in random replay retains overall performance while achieving the lowest tail error. Structured CoT (think variant) helps continuous waypoint generation, especially on real-world transfer (ADE 0.953 -> 0.619).
method: Video curation: ~500h of street-walking video from 30 cities/15 countries, cut into 5-min clips, VLM filtering of cuts, subject-focused clips, doorways/stairs/elevators

Trajectory reconstruction: LoGeR with Pi3X backbone gives metric camera poses, projected to ground plane, sampled at 1 Hz into 10-frame episodes (5 past, 5 future); 20 rule-based meta-actions from speed/lateral progress/direction

CoT annotation: GroundingDINO + reconstructed depth give object/location/depth labels; Qwen3.6VL-27B teacher writes perception-analysis-planning rationale, with future frames and meta-action used only as privileged verification

WILD-Nav model: Qwen3.5VL-4B with frozen vision encoder; <PLAN_QUERY> token hidden state feeds a linear meta-action head and a 4-layer MLP trajectory head (5 waypoints); think variant generates rationale first, inst variant places token before the rationale
Multi-task loss: CoT LM loss + meta-action cross-entropy + waypoint MSE, with higher LR for action expert than LM adapters

Long-tail characterization: episode rarity via smoothed IDF over joint object/spatial/motion features; difficulty via top-3% ADE union top-3% FDE; hard set analysed by SVD+UMAP+HDBSCAN clustering and teacher reflection for failure attribution

setting.backbone: Qwen3.5VL-4B (fine-tuned, frozen vision encoder) + MLP action heads
setting.training_data: ~500h in-the-wild street-walking video, >500K auto-annotated samples (80/20 train/test split); real-world data (SCAND, SiT, GND; 45096 samples) only in fine-tuning experiments
setting.observation: monocular RGB current frame + 4 past frames + past 2D trajectory + local 2D point goal
setting.action_space: 5 predicted ground-plane waypoints plus a discrete meta-action (20 classes)
setting.privileged: none at test time (future observations and reference trajectory used only for annotation and reflection analysis)

results: WILD-Nav-inst cuts all planning errors by at least 53.4% versus fine-tuned SocialNav on the video test set and FDE by 47.8% versus UrbanNav; the think variant is best (ADE 0.086, FDE 0.068). After real-world fine-tuning, WILD-Nav-inst reduces FDE and MAOE by 55.6% and 45.8% relative to UrbanNav. Hard+random fine-tuning gives the lowest tail errors while preserving overall performance.
limitations: Real-world evaluation is offline ADE/FDE plus qualitative robot trials only, with no closed-loop quantitative navigation success metrics
Domain gap persists between video and real-world data even after fine-tuning; the real-world training set is small
Failure attributions are statistical associations from teacher-VLM reflection, not exhaustive causal categories, and depend on reconstructed trajectories (pseudo-labels)
